question: How do the deployed public-goods funding protocols (Gitcoin Grants Stack and Allo, Optimism Retro Funding, Hypercerts, Protocol Guild, clr.fund and MACI, Flow State Flow Councils, Thrive, Celo Prosperity Pass, Nouns, Kleros, Hats, Metagov, Funding the Commons) allocate funds at the contract level, at what scale, and where do they stop?

frame.population: deployed public-goods funding protocols and their governing organisations
frame.exposure: first-party source code, deployed contracts, documentation, governance-forum posts, DeFiLlama reads and academic evaluations, read 2026-10-08
frame.comparator: quadratic funding as specified by Buterin, Hitzig and Weyl

findings.finding: Allo charges the percent fee on every fundPool call and routes it to the treasury; the base fee is paid in native token on pool creation.

findings.finding: Strategy directories in contracts/strategies: direct-allocation, direct-grants-lite, donation-voting-merkle-base, donation-voting-merkle-distribution-direct-transfer, donation-voting-merkle-distribution-vault, easy-rpgf, ltip-hedgey, ltip-hedgey-governor, ltip-simple, qv-base, qv-simple, rfp-committee, rfp-simple, plus a _poc folder (micro-grants, sqf-superfluid, qv-impact-stream, hedgey, sablier-v2, proportional-payout and others).

The on-chain QV strategy computes a donor's votes to a recipient as the square root of the voice credits they put on it and pays each recipient the pool times its share of summed votes; recipient votes are a sum of per-allocator square roots, not the square of that sum, so the Buterin-Hitzig-Weyl cross-term matching is not computed on-chain by this strategy.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 voteResult = _sqrt(totalCredits * 1e18);

findings.finding: QV payout is pro-rata on summed votes.

item.title: gitcoinco/qf-calculator (last commit 2025-05-20)

findings.finding: The calculator that computes Gitcoin matching off-chain implements standard QF as the square of summed square-roots minus the donations.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: funding = {p: (donation_df[p].apply(lambda x: sqrt(x)).sum() ** 2) - donation_df[p].sum() for p in projects}

findings.finding: It also implements pairwise matching with coefficient k_ij = M / (M + sqrt_i . sqrt_j), cluster match, and COCM with calcstyle 'markov', 'og' or 'pct_friends' (a friendship matrix between donors built from shared cluster membership).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: k_matrix = M / (M + sqrt_donation_df.dot(sqrt_donation_df.transpose()))

findings.finding: Passport scores gate donations in the calculator: a donation is dropped if the donor's score is below score_at_50_percent, the amount is below a minimum, or it is a self-vote; amounts scale linearly from 0.5x at the 50% score to 1.0x at the 100% score.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: scale_range = np.array([0.5, 1.0])

item.title: Lessons learned from two years of Retroactive Public Goods Funding (ccerv1, Optimism governance forum, 2024-11-05)

findings.finding: The OSO author reports that mega rounds devolved into popularity contests and that there is no data yet showing retroactive funding produces superior outcomes.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: We've learned that mega rounds devolve into popularity contests and annual feedback loops are too slow.

findings.finding: Same post: measurement.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The not-so-good news is that we don’t (yet) have the data to show that retroactive funding produces superior outcomes.

findings.finding: Round 3: any project could sign up, projects needed 17 votes, over 600 approved, voters overwhelmed, onchain projects got a smaller share than badgeholders felt they deserved. Round 4: metrics-based voting, over 200 of 400+ applicants approved, steep power law. Round 5: expert-grouped project voting, flat results, perverse incentive to split work across more teams.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Perverse incentive to divide work across multiple smaller contributions / teams in order to receive more tokens.

findings.finding: Lessons: humans are good at relative comparisons and bad at outright comparisons; data is good at coverage of countable things and bad at nuance.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Humans are good at relative comparisons (what’s more valuable)

item.title: clrfund/monorepo contracts (last commit 2024-07-31, repo pushed 2024-08-01)

findings.finding: FundingRound.sol: contributors contribute tokens and receive MACI voice credits (MAX_VOICE_CREDITS 1e9, max contribution 1e4 tokens, voiceCreditFactor derived); votes are cast as encrypted MACI messages; the coordinator tallies with zk proofs and the contract verifies tally and spent credits in finalize().
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 private constant MAX_VOICE_CREDITS = 10 ** 9;  // MACI allows 2 ** 32 voice credits max

findings.finding: Payout is capital-constrained QF with an alpha: allocated = (alpha * (votes^2) + (precision - alpha) * spent) / precision, alpha = (budget - contributions) / (voiceCreditFactor * (sum of squared votes - total spent)), per Buterin-Hitzig-Weyl page 17; finalize reverts if no project has more than one vote.

item.title: A Flexible Design for Funding Public Goods

findings.finding: Quadratic funding: project receives the square of the sum of the square roots of contributions; first best under the standard model; variations limit cost and protect against collusion.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The amount received by the project is (proportional to) the square of the sum of the square roots of contributions received.

item.title: Quadratic Funding and Matching Funds Requirements

findings.finding: Using Gitcoin Grants data, matching requirements scale rapidly and are exhausted early; contributors give small amounts scattered across projects; significant reciprocal backing is found.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: we also identify a significant amount of reciprocal backing, which could be consistent with the kind of strategic behavior we discuss.

item.title: A Social Choice Analysis of Optimism's Retroactive Project Funding

findings.finding: Four rounds had allocated over $100M with $1.3B reserved; the authors identify significant shortcomings in the allocation system and recommend the utilitarian moving phantoms mechanism, which is strategyproof.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: we identify significant shortcomings in the current allocation system

item.title: Evaluating Voting Design Vulnerabilities for Retroactive Funding

findings.finding: Proof-based analysis plus voting simulations of vulnerabilities in the quadratic, mean and median voting schemes used for Optimism RetroPGF.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: We present a proof-based formal analysis for vulnerabilities in these voting schemes, empirically validate these vulnerabilities using voting simulations
